title: Finite open exchange commutes with coefficient restriction and tower transitions
statement:
Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow X,j':U'\hookrightarrow X',g:X'\to X,g_U:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], and let $a:B\to C$ be any homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, the inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_a$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and exact sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let
$$\beta_B:g_B^*j_!^B\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^B g_{U,B}^*,\qquad \beta_C:g_C^*j_!^C\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^C g_{U,C}^*$$
be the canonical complex-level exchanges of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], using finite constant-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The canonical scalar-restriction identifications for the inverse images and extensions identify
$$\operatorname{Res}_a(\beta_{C,F})=\beta_{B,\operatorname{Res}_aF}$$
for every complex $F$ of $C$-module sheaves on $U$. Under these identifications the units and counits defining the inverse adjoint mates also agree: $\beta_B^{-1}$ is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ adjunct of
$$g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{g_U^{-1}u_F}g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\cong j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F,$$
where $u$ is the extension/restriction unit and the last map is the adjunction-compatible site-composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. All these assertions are natural in chain maps and in $a$, including identities and composites. In particular, for any sequence of finite rings $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ and complexes $F_n$ with strict $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}F_n$, the maps $\beta_{B_n,F_n}$ and their inverses commute with every transition and define inverse maps of the underlying strict towers of abelian sheaf complexes. They also do so as towers over a ring sheaf acting through compatible maps to the $(B_n)$ coefficient sheaves. No quasi-compactness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For openResMap invertibility, use the proved fixedRestriction equivalence from constant-ring module sheaves to sheaves of modules over the constant ring. The coefficient comparison resFixed is identity on underlying sections, with scalar linearity following from naturality of the sheafification unit. Define fixedPull as the mate of fixedDirect and prove the scalar pullback square by taking direct-image mates, where all maps are identity on sections. In ordinary module-sheaf coordinates the inverse open mate is invertible by scalarOpenModel_isIso. Invert the pasted pullback square and take inverse mates under the open adjunctions. Transport across resFixed, then cancel the fixedPull inverse mate, which is invertible because its horizontal edges are equivalences. This proves that the originally specified openResMap is invertible, without changing any adjunction or functor. The standard mate-unit and mate-counit equations give open_unit_counit and pull_unit_counit.

proof.text: The proved degreewise component theorem compares the actual inverse exchanges by their open-adjunction adjuncts, using scalar-unit compatibility and the normalized square-compositor identity. Canceling the invertible exchanges gives the forward square. Naturality in chain maps and in coefficient maps follows from the specified natural transformations and the identity/composition mate equations. No alternate base-change map is substituted.

proof.text: In Lean, beta is the inverse of asIso singleBetaInv, and betaC is its termwise lift to complexes. Its inverse component in degree i therefore reduces to singleBetaInvApp at F.X i. By the definition of singleBetaInvApp from [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], this is exactly the transpose of the pulled-back open unit followed by the inverse moduleSquareG comparison. Thus inverse_unit_transpose follows definitionally, with no further mate calculation.

For a semilinear chain map t:F -> Res_a G, specialize exchange_restrictScalars at G. Compose the resulting square with the inverse exchange and cancel the invertible B-exchange to obtain the inverse scalar square. Naturality of the B-exchange and its inverse at t, followed by the two scalar squares, proves exchange_transition. For the strict and ambient tower assertions, apply the forgetful or ambient restriction functor to these successor equalities. Naturality of resForget or ambientRes transports the final coefficient comparison, yielding the required successor square. NatTrans.ofOpSequence constructs the forward and inverse tower maps. The component inverse identities prove that they are inverse, and the naturality constructor extends the successor equalities to every tower arrow.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q49-fe9d5b3b0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full, all 9 cited statements, the full proofs of lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change and lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero, the parent lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison (its step 8 applies the item to P_b->P_a; steps 9 and 11 rely on the inverse-mate normalization), the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof, Stacks 03DI (sites-modules.tex l.2058), and the unit and chapter records. The statement is true and keeps the parent's coefficient category (constant finite commutative rings, small pro-etale sites). beta runs g^{-1}j_! -> j'_!g_U^{-1} as in the base-change node, and the stated inverse mate is the correct one. No qc or constructibility hypothesis is needed. Small cases checked: a=id, zero ring, U empty, U=X, g=id, one-level tower, Z/l^n quotient towers. Not a duplicate: the base-change node has one ring; the underived-compatibility node gives the same mate normalization but on the etale site; strict-tower-proper-open-calculus has one fixed ring B; and no clause of the parent is restated. Faults, both E5: step 3 transported beta summand by summand and invoked an unnamed uniqueness, and step 4 asserted the mate computation without doing it. The fix rewrites steps 1-4 only. Step 1 adds h_* and the units and counits of h^* -| h_*. Step 2 shows the units and adjuncts are ring-independent, citing the 03DI construction. Step 3 now uses the Beck-Chevalley characterization: beta is the unique map with adjunct t^{-1}eta_2, where t_{M,V}=M(a_V) and Res_a fixes t and the units. Step 4 computes the j'_!-adjunct of beta^{-1} as sigma o g_U^{-1}u_F, with sigma the mate of t, and identifies sigma with the composition comparison via clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition. I read the statement's 'canonical map' as the standard Beck-Chevalley exchange constructed in step 6 of the base-change node. The statement, stmt_deps and proof_deps union are unchanged, every step is under 2000 characters, and there is no cycle. Both declared tool_uses are accepted (prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact, lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition). No SGA, no new nodes, nothing dropped.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
